title.narrative: Transformation Approach to Large Scale Investment in Support of the Implementation of the Great Green Wall (TALSIG)

description.narrative: Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

To build a coordinated framework that advances green and sustainable development in the GGW Region by strengthening capacities, promoting resilient livelihoods, restoring natural resources, and enhancing regional adaptation.

X Yes Thorough environmental and social evaluations are essential upon promoting sub-projects. Therefore, it will be crucial to involve the IPLC, ensuring they give their free, prior, and informed consent, especially when pinpointing alternative avenues for enhanced livelihoods and other related activities. Stakeholders, including affected communities, have been informed of the project and its grievance redress mechanism during the inception workshops, as well as through multiple channels, including community meetings, newsletters, and the project website. The Regional Project will support the national child projects on how to establish and manage a grievance mechanism. Populations will play a central role in the enforcement of the Project. Not only as beneficiaries, but also as proactive stakeholders. Their commitment in the restauration of the Land will be key. Thereof, specific attention to socio-economic dimensions has been given to Project design from the very beginning. Tables 13 and 14 illustrate how the Project aims at enhancing socio-economic benefits for the populations of the GGW region. Table 13: Principles followed in the project designers that will directly or/and indirectly support socio-economic benefits Principles followed in the project design that will directly or/and indirectly support socio-economic benefits The project aims to be inclusive and responsive to the needs and concerns of these stakeholders throughout its lifecycle. Concerns related to gender equality and human rights will be actively addressed through targeted interventions and will be continually monitored throughout the project to ensure that they are adequately resolved. Program team and steering committees have been structured to ensure gender-balanced representation. Gender considerations have been integrated into the design of each child project and will continue to be a focus during implementation. A gender gap analysis was conducted during the program's planning phase, and a gender-responsive approach has been adopted. This will serve as the foundation for a more detailed gender action plan that will be developed as the project progresses. The program is designed to provide long-term environmental, social, and economic benefits by promoting sustainable land management and livelihoods. It aims to avoid any short-term gains that could lead to long-term burdens. The program and its child projects are committed to ensuring that economic benefits are equitably distributed. Special attention is being given to marginalized and vulnerable groups to ensure that they are not excluded from the benefits generated by the project. The program will support sustainable agricultural and livelihood practices that are designed to be beneficial for agriculture dependent people (farmers, NWFP harvesters, livestock breeders, etc.). This aligns with the program's objective of promoting equitable and diversified resilient livelihood opportunities. The program aims to increase the resilience of local communities through its various interventions, including sustainable land management and livelihood diversification, thereby reducing their vulnerability to climate change and disaster risks. The program aims to enhance the sustainable management of natural resources, thereby positively impacting community health and safety. The program will support indigenous peoples' access to rights and resources, aligning with its objectives of promoting equitable and diversified resilient livelihood opportunities. The program will support the establishment of livelihood support mechanisms to provide alternative livelihood options for local communities, including indigenous peoples. The program aims to respect and preserve the cultural heritage of indigenous peoples, aligning with its objectives of promoting equitable and diversified resilient livelihood opportunities. The program aims to create enabling conditions for sustainable development, which will result in long-term environmental, social, and economic benefits, including increased employment. The program aims to integrate issues of gender parity and inclusiveness, aligning with its objectives of promoting equitable and diversified resilient livelihood opportunities.
